2 يبّسهُ , (S, A, K;) inf. n. تَيْبِيسٌ, (S,) He dried it; made it dry; [&c.; see 1;] (S, A, K;) as also ↓ أَيْبَسَهُ . (M, A, K.) ―
-b2- [Hence the saying,] أُعِيذُكَ بِٱللّٰهِ أَنْ تُيَبِّسَ رَحِمًا مَبْلُولَةً (tropical:) [I pray that thou mayest be preserved by God from thy withering a freshened tie of relationship]. (A, TA.) And لَا تُوبِسِ الثَّرَى بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَكَ (tropical:) [Wither not the fresh and vigorous friendship, between me and thee; i. e., sever not thou the firm bond of friendship that unites me and thee: see يَبِسَ مَا بَيْنَهُمَا; and see also ثَرًى]. (A, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
